correctness.rationale: For b>=2,n>=5 the semigroup is numerical since gcd(R_n,R_(n+1))=1. The exchange moves for {1,q=b+1,h=b²+b+1} terminate at the unique minimum-coin greedy form L(t). The exact generator identity R_(n+j)=a+c R_j for j=1,2,3 (c=(b−1)a+1) and L(t+1)−L(t) in {1,1−b} give strictly increasing W(t)=aL(t)+ct and Apéry(S,a)={W(t):0<=t<a}. For the semigroup order, an Apéry domination by a nonzero sum of non-a generators cannot wrap in t since L(u)<a<c and must yield a one-coin increase; conversely a one-coin increase gives direct domination. Hence maximal candidates lie in the terminal h-slab. With a mod h=0,1,q according to n mod 3, the complete maximal indices are (a−2,a−1), (a−3,a−2,a−1), and (a−q−2,a−1). Their W differences yield the claimed {F,F−1}, {F,F−1,F−2}, and {F,F−(R_(n+2)+1)} sets. Independent exact Dijkstra residue computation, independent of the repository checker, matched all Apéry representatives and PF sets in 270 generic residue inputs and 21 actual repunit instances. These finite tests support, but do not prove, the all-b,n statement. A sentence in the terminal-slab exposition describes the +1 screening too narrowly; the combined +1/+q inequalities, separately checked, deliver the correct complete candidate table.

value.rationale: The semigroups generated by the first four consecutive repunits after a chosen length are a natural truncation of the classic repunit numerical-semigroup family, and pseudo-Frobenius type and gap spacing are standard structural invariants. The uniform exact mod-three 2/3/2 type law and especially the unbounded nonconsecutive gap R_(n+2)+1 expose a meaningful boundary phenomenon not determined for b>=3 by the published divisible and Mersenne special cases. The motivation is independent of finite verification and does not depend on promising a new broad theorem or an external application; the previously known b=2 and n divisible by 3 cases are credited.
